summary: BioPulse–Twin is a browser-based research prototype for astronaut health monitoring. Users record health indicators, compare changes with personal references, choose research support options and reassess their observations. The application combines local records with NASA research archives and inspectable physiological scenarios. Core functions work offline in a single HTML file. A contextual heart-rate method achieved an F1-score of 0.744 on injected changes in MMASH reference data. The prototype supports investigation and self-monitoring, with clinical and astronaut validation still required.
details: BioPulse–Twin addresses the challenge “Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions.” Our team, MINOR, consists of Ceren Aygün, Cemal Bayram and Aybars Tutumlu. PURPOSE Long-duration missions require astronauts to monitor physical and behavioral changes with limited access to immediate ground support. BioPulse–Twin provides a local workflow for recording observations, inspecting changes, selecting support options and reviewing subsequent measurements. USER WORKFLOW Users enter measurements with timestamps, units, sources and measurement conditions. The software separates personal observations from synthetic demonstration records and published research data. Personal references use comparable prior observations. The robust fallback requires at least eight eligible records and uses the median and median absolute deviation. Ordinal self-reports use observed reference ranges. Missing values and zero dispersion do not receive an invented standardized score. Users can inspect findings, review source-informed support options, record sessions and repeat comparable measurements. Equipment and user-declared mission clearance gate physical activities. Changes after an activity do not establish treatment efficacy. NASA DATA AND SCIENTIFIC CONTEXT The application includes 758 NASA reference observations: 182 RadLab instrument records, 364 blood observations, 147 biomarker observations and 65 mouse bone observations. Source units, study identities and processing records remain inspectable. RadLab measurements support instrument-specific dose integration. OSDR data provide blood, biomarker and bone reference views. Research participants and animal observations remain separate from the personal profile. An anatomical explorer connects reference structures with bone, radiation, DNA repair and cerebrospinal-fluid scenario tools. Uncalibrated parameters remain explicit, and unsupported immune predictions remain disabled. IMPLEMENTATION AND EVALUATION The application uses HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with embedded assets and local browser storage. Core operation requires no installation or external generative AI service. Users can import and export records as CSV or JSON. The contextual heart-rate candidate uses clock time, steps and lying fraction when compatible measurements exist. An evaluation across 22 MMASH participants used leave-one-subject-out folds, chronological personal training data and identical injection and missingness conditions. At zero missingness, the candidate achieved precision 0.737, recall 0.750 and F1 0.744, detecting 19 of 22 injected events. These results concern synthetic +35 bpm changes added to terrestrial reference data. They do not establish clinical anomaly accuracy or astronaut performance. The deployed rolling reference also differs from the frozen evaluation setup. AI ASSISTANCE AND ATTRIBUTION OpenAI ChatGPT/Codex assisted coding, debugging, source retrieval, analysis, verification and preparation of project text and slides. The application distinguishes observed data, synthetic examples and mathematical scenarios. Scientific Evidence contains source references, third-party credits and licence records, including unresolved permissions for some supplied models. The prototype provides research support. Clinical decisions remain with mission medical personnel.
